patch.value: GH-1004: history-repair remains writer-version-specific across 2026.8.7 and 2026.8.13

A real post-epoch reproduction shows genuine drift repaired by pm 2026.8.7 is accepted only by that reader, while repair by 2026.8.13 is accepted only by the newer reader; alternating the supported CLIs rewrites the same stream indefinitely and each reports the other's bytes as hash/chain drift.

A cross-version fixture reproduces the two-writer loop; repair converges or refuses without rewriting an internally consistent supported epoch; diagnostics attribute version incompatibility instead of generic corruption; focused and repository-wide exact coverage remain green
On one drifted tracker, alternate published 2026.8.7 and 2026.8.13 history-repair --all, running each version's health --strict-exit after each rewrite as documented in GitHub #1004.
Supported readers either accept one converged repaired representation or the repair command refuses a writer-version-only rewrite with an actionable compatibility diagnostic.
Repair under 2026.8.7 makes 2026.8.13 fail strict health; repair under 2026.8.13 makes 2026.8.7 fail, and the files differ byte-for-byte.
Pinned CI and global agents can disagree on identical bytes and repeatedly rewrite append-only evidence while following the documented remediation.
